title: CI macOS: a lane fails with every test ok when bats-core 1.14.0's parallel forwarder loses a child's status (bats-exec-file:195)
body:
## What happened

Candidate CI run 43248401461 (release commit 61dbd245, since reset) went red on macOS alone. All 3136 tests printed ok. One file's within-file parallel forwarder then failed at bats-core 1.14.0 `bats-exec-file:195`, `wait "$(cat .../pid)"`, with "wait: pid 47349 is not a child of this shell", and the lane exited 1. Ubuntu and WSL 2 were green on the same commit. The log is kept at ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/0.1.23/ci-macos-61dbd245.log.

## Why it matters

A red with no failing test costs a whole cut attempt: the 0.1.23 cut was resumed and then re-cut after it.

## Not yet known

Whether the cause is bash reaping the child before the forwarder's wait (the same family as 0342, where bash dropped a process substitution's status under 24 jobs), and whether it depends on the job count. The run that failed used the floor of 24 jobs on a 3-CPU runner; since 0340-3 CI uses the runner's own CPU count.

## Options, none chosen

- Read whether a newer bats-core changes that wait.
- Have the lane runner treat a file whose TAP is complete and all ok as green when the forwarder alone fails, and say so in the seal.
- Leave it, if it does not recur at the runner's own CPU count.

## Resolution

Fixed in one landing on main, 627f700a07ed20fbed7a5f6032d517fc4cb4fb10 (2026-11-13 09:34Z), unit 0347-1 from the tested tip 29af779f, in devbin 0.1.24's batch; unpushed until devbin's next cut. It was proved on its own arms under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 (red at the base's code, green at the fix) on devbin-vc's desk. hv took the second option.

- Cause: bats-core#1278 (open) is this failure. In parallel mode, bats forwards each test's output in start order and only then waits for its pid. By then bash has reaped a test that ended early and holds its status in its saved list, and bash drops that status when a later fork is given the same pid. The wait then fails with "not a child of this shell", and the file exits 1 though every test printed ok. macOS's pid_max of 99998 wraps within a long suite; Linux's 4194304 rarely does, which is why only macOS went red.
- A newer bats-core: none yet. 1.14.0 (2026-07-21) is the latest release. The upstream fix, bats-core#1281 (open, not merged), records each test's status in a file and makes the wait best-effort. Once a release carries it, the gate below never matches.
- The fix, in lib/bats-lanes's recorder, which already wraps each file of the parallel lane: it holds the file's stdout and stderr and passes them on whole, as GNU parallel's grouping does.
  - A file that exits non-zero is counted green only when all three hold: its stderr carries bash's "wait: pid N is not a child of this shell", its stdout has no `not ok`, and it has an `ok` for every test the list gives it.
  - Its line among the times says so beside its exit, and a line before the verdict counts such files.
  - Any other failure keeps its exit.

Three new arms in testhandler.bats drive the forwarder's failure through a BASH_ENV `wait` that fails only where bats forwards a test's results:
- (a) an all-ok file is counted green, and the run says so;
- (b) a file with a failed test stays red;
- (c) a forwarder that fails without bash's words keeps the file red.

(a) was red at the base; (b) and (c) hold that a red stays red, so they are green there by construction. The 17 lanes arms were green at the fix under BSD and GNU. 0.1.24's note carries it under Fixed.
